props.gloss_en: one who ate and forgot and did not bless -- Beit Shammai: he returns to his place and blesses
Beit Hillel: he blesses in the place where he remembered
Rav Zevid: the dispute [of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel over one who ate and did not bless] is where he forgot
Rav Zevid: but where he did it deliberately, all agree he returns to his place and blesses
you might have said: the same [Beit Hillel's ruling] holds even where he did it deliberately
and that [the mishnah] teaches 'and forgot' is to tell you the strength of Beit Shammai's view
Beit Hillel to Beit Shammai: by your words, one who ate atop the Bira, forgot, and descended without blessing must go back up to the top of the Bira and bless?!
Beit Shammai to Beit Hillel: by your words, one who forgot his purse atop the Bira -- will he not go up and take it?
one student, [who had not blessed] unwittingly, did as Beit Shammai and found a purse of gold
and one, [who had not blessed] deliberately, did as Beit Hillel, and a lion ate him
Rabba bar bar Chana was travelling in a caravan; he ate, forgot, and did not bless
Rabba bar bar Chana: what shall I do? If I tell them 'I forgot to bless' they will say 'bless [here] -- wherever you bless, you bless the Merciful One'; better I tell them 'I forgot a golden dove'
he told them 'wait for me, for I forgot a golden dove', went [back] and blessed, and found a golden dove
why a dove? because the community of Israel is likened to a dove
as it is written: 'the wings of a dove covered with silver, and its pinions with the shimmer of gold' (Ps 68:14)
as a dove is saved only by its wings, so Israel is saved only by the mitzvot
